_README.purpose: Ingest queries, one entry per therapeutic area. Read by ingest/pull_trials.py to build CT.gov API v2 queries, and by tests/test_coverage.py to verify every term below actually returns trials.
_README.combine: Controls how condition/pathogen terms relate to intervention terms. 'or' issues SEPARATE queries per term group and unions the results. 'and' requires a trial to match both groups in one query, which is what v1 did. v2 defaults to 'or' -- see the note below, this is a deliberate change.
_README.why_or_not_and: v1 sent query.cond AND query.intr in a single request, so a trial had to match both a listed condition AND a listed intervention to be ingested at all. That systematically excluded any trial whose intervention is a development code rather than a known drug name -- APX001, F901318, SPR720. Those are novel assets, which are the single most competitively interesting rows in a landscape view. v1's ingest was quietly filtering out the trials the tool exists to find. v2 casts a wide net at ingest (recall) and does the precision work in retrieve/ via structured scoring (precision). Conflating the two stages is what caused the gap.
_README.pathogen_terms: Queried against the condition field alongside condition_terms, but tracked separately because pathogen is a first-class retrieval criterion in anti-infectives, not a synonym for indication. Two trials both labelled 'pneumonia' can be in unrelated competitive markets depending on the organism and its resistance profile. See docs/SCOPE-v2.md, correction #5.
_README.term_accuracy: Every intervention term is a real compound. tests/test_coverage.py asserts non-zero registry hits for each one, so a typo or a discontinued code name fails a test rather than silently narrowing the corpus -- which is how v1 bug #6 hid.

antifungals.description: Antifungal trials. v1's seed area, kept under the same key so existing trial_areas rows remain valid.

antibacterials.description: Antibacterial trials, including the WHO priority resistant-organism space and TB.
condition_terms: acute bacterial skin and skin structure infection

antivirals.description: Antiviral trials: respiratory, hepatitis, HIV, and transplant-associated viral disease.
